column1: # LearnLife NFC Attender — flash layout (4 MB ESP32-WROOM-32)
# ⚠ THIS CAN ONLY BE APPLIED OVER USB. A partition table cannot be changed by
#   an OTA update
column2: because the running firmware lives inside the layout it

column1: #   would be rewriting. Flash this during assembly
#   either one goes to the Hub — otherwise the only way to change it later is
#   to open the enclosure and connect a cable.
# ── WHY THE DEFAULT TABLE DOESN'T WORK ───────────────────────────────────
# Arduino's default ESP32 layout gives each of the two app slots 1280 KB. The
# build is already ~1.11 MB
column3: and OTA support plus the pinned

column1: # CA certificates only add to it. Running out of app space is not a graceful
# failure — the link succeeds locally and the OTA write fails on the device.
# So: 1536 KB per slot
column2: which puts the current image at ~72% and leaves real

column1: # headroom. The space comes out of the filesystem
column2: which has far more than it

column1: # needs.
# app0 and app1 are a matched pair. The device runs from one and writes the
# incoming update into the other
column2: then flips `otadata` to point at it and

column1: # reboots. If the new image doesn't boot
column2: the bootloader can roll back to the

column1: # slot that still holds the working firmware. That redundancy is the whole
# reason a bricked update isn't a trip to the Hub with a laptop — and it is
# why the two slots must be the same size.
# ── WHAT SURVIVES A REPARTITION
# nvs stays at 0x9000 with the same size
# credentials
column3: and the device id are all still

column1: # there after reflashing. You do not have to re-run the captive portal.
# The filesystem partition MOVES
column2: so its contents are LOST and it is

column1: # reformatted on first boot (main.cpp mounts with formatOnFail=true). That
# means /roster.txt
#   -> The roster and today-cache re-fetch automatically. No action needed.
#   -> The QUEUE DOES NOT. Any scans still waiting to reach PocketBase are
#      destroyed. Before repartitioning a device that has been in service
#      bring it online and check `q` on the serial console reads 0 pending.
#   0x009000  nvs        20 KB   provisioning — unchanged from default
#   0x00e000  otadata     8 KB   which app slot to boot
#   0x010000  app0     1536 KB   firmware slot A
#   0x190000  app1     1536 KB   firmware slot B (OTA target)
#   0x310000  spiffs    896 KB   roster
#   0x3f0000  coredump   64 KB   panic dumps
# App partitions must start on a 64 KB boundary; data partitions on 4 KB.
# Offsets above satisfy both and tile the 4 MB exactly with no gaps.
# The filesystem row is NAMED "spiffs" even though it holds LittleFS
# is deliberate. Arduino's LittleFS.begin() selects the partition by LABEL
# defaulting to "spiffs"; the SubType column has no littlefs value to use
# instead. Naming it "littlefs" reads better and silently breaks the mount —
# esp_littlefs reports `partition "spiffs" could not be found`
# into the formatOnFail path
column3: and the device runs with no

column1: # persistence at all: no durable queue
